newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Tuesday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt lower in light volume amid stiff resistance from packers who are dealing with unprofitable operating margins, livestock sources said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 lower at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants in light trading, packer buyers and dealers there said.

Illinois hogs sold $0.50 lower at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants. Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants, sources there said.
Packer margins slipped deeper in the red on Monday as cash hog prices were steady to $0.50 higher and pork prices were lower, the dealers said.
Estimated gross cutout values of a 175-lb hog carcass based on USDA cutting yield tests and carlot prices Monday were quoted down $0.30 to $0.31.
Declines in pork prices were led by weak fresh ham, butt and pork belly prices, which overshadowed strength in lean trimmings, USDA statistics showed.
